text:
Mattias Samuelsson is playing 23 minutes a night on a Buffalo team that has lost too often lately. He had a maintenance day this week and was back on the ice for the morning skate, and he scored early in a loss at Philadelphia, near where he grew up.

His season is steady more than spectacular: three goals and 13 points in 24 games, none on the power play, 44 blocked shots and 30 hits. His point rate sits right in the middle of his talent range. The Sabres are about even with him on at five on five (49% of the expected goals), close to their rate without him. Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among all defensemen in wins above replacement last season, a reminder that his value is in the minutes he soaks up, not the box score. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him exiting the zone with possession 49% of the time. Our range projects 35 to 52 points. For a team trying to climb back into the race, he's the steady piece.
